LESSON: MELODY

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Creating and Executing
Topic 1.5: Melody

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Melody. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it necessary to apply composition techniques in composing a melody?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. sing the sol-fa syllables d r m f s for pitch discrimination
2. compose short melodies based on the sol-fa syllables d r m f s
3. appreciate melodies created by self and others

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: MELODY
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Melody helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: MELODY
Study Melody like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Sing the sol-fa syllables d r m f s for pitch discrimination

What this means
In this part you learn to sing the sol-fa syllables d r m f s for pitch discrimination. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: sing the sol-fa syllables d r m f s for pitch discrimination.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Melody” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can sing the sol-fa syllables d r m f s for pitch discrimination. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Compose short melodies based on the sol-fa syllables d r m f s

What this means
In this part you learn to compose short melodies based on the sol-fa syllables d r m f s. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: compose short melodies based on the sol-fa syllables d r m f s.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Melody in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can compose short melodies based on the sol-fa syllables d r m f s. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate melodies created by self and others

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate melodies created by self and others. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate melodies created by self and others.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate melodies created by self and others. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Melody is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Melody” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: sing the sol-fa syllables d r m f s for pitch discrimination)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Melody in your own words. (skill: compose short melodies based on the sol-fa syllables d r m f s)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: appreciate melodies created by self and others)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Melody to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: sing the sol-fa syllables d r m f s for pitch discrimination.
3. Practise this skill: compose short melodies based on the sol-fa syllables d r m f s.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate melodies created by self and others.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Melody from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Melody: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Melody?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it necessary to apply composition techniques in composing a melody?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Melody means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: sing the sol-fa syllables d r m f s for pitch discrimination.
5. Be able to: compose short melodies based on the sol-fa syllables d r m f s.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
